goal: Reduce repeated Owner approvals without weakening governance. Today every project asks again for the same low-risk external connections (e.g. official public read-only data). Approved low-risk scope should be reusable; anything materially riskier must still ask.
task: Create axbranch/permissions.py with: (1) RISKS = ('public_read', 'api_key', 'login', 'paid', 'personal_data', 'posting'), ordered low→high; only 'public_read' may ever be reused. (2) classify(entry) -> risk: start from entry.get('risk') (default 'public_read' if missing), then ESCALATE deterministically when the domain/purpose text indicates more risk: words like key/token/apikey -> 'api_key'; login/account/oauth/password -> 'login'; paid/subscription/billing/price plan -> 'paid'; email/personal/user data/upload -> 'personal_data'; post/publish/send/tweet/trade/order -> 'posting'. Never downgrade a declared risk. (3) A standing-permission store in the same SQLite file, owned by this module: table standing_permissions(domain TEXT, risk TEXT, granted REAL, project_id TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(domain, risk)), created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS via store.db. (4) grant(store, pid, entries): record standing grants for every approved entry whose classified risk is 'public_read' (others are never stored) and add a store.event(pid, 'permission_granted', domains=[...], risk='public_read'). (5) evaluate(store, entries) -> {'reused': [...], 'ask': [...]}: an entry is reused only if classify(entry)=='public_read' AND its domain (lower-cased, exact match) has a standing public_read grant; everything else goes to 'ask'. Tests in tests/test_permissions.py covering: reuse of an approved public_read domain in a later project; no reuse for a different domain; escalation by keywords (an approved domain whose new purpose mentions an API key or login must ask again); declared higher risk is never reused even if the domain was approved as public_read; grant never stores non-public_read; risk ordering.
contract: Entries are dicts {domain, purpose, risk?} as in a plan's network_access. store is axbranch.state.Store (use store.db for SQL and store.event for events; do not modify state.py). Public API exactly: RISKS, classify(entry), grant(store, pid, entries), evaluate(store, entries). Standard library only.
constraints: Do not touch other files (the lead integrates it into engine.py). Escalation must be conservative: when in doubt, ask. Keep it small and readable.
expected_output: axbranch/permissions.py and tests/test_permissions.py; full suite passing.
